subject.title: fix(diagnostics): evict orphaned tool/model activity on owner-less run end

question: After a current-main rebase, should OpenClaw accept owner-less eviction of tool/model diagnostic markers plus the new operator-visible telemetry counters as the canonical cleanup boundary?
rationale: The implementation is narrowly targeted and proof-positive, but the correct ownership invariant determines whether future session recovery protects or disrupts active work; that tradeoff requires maintainer acceptance at the refreshed merge result.

options.title: Rebase, validate, and accept the boundary
options.body: Refresh the branch onto current main, keep the inner-owner and late-start safeguards, and merge if focused diagnostics/exporter checks confirm the same behavior.

options.title: Require production-shape proof
options.body: Request a redacted live gateway/channel artifact if maintainers need confirmation beyond the supplied real in-process runtime proof.

options.title: Pause for a broader recovery design
options.body: Defer this PR if maintainers want one unified stale-activity recovery design rather than this focused reply-run cleanup.

recommendation.title: Rebase, validate, and accept the boundary
recommendation.body: Refresh the branch onto current main, keep the inner-owner and late-start safeguards, and merge if focused diagnostics/exporter checks confirm the same behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: This account is assigned on the PR and has adjacent history on the recovered-owner cutoff mechanism reused by the patch.
